sections.h2: Who answers questions about a Madison County, KY tax bill?
sections.html:
Three Richmond offices split the work. The sheriff answers for the bill, the PVA answers for the value behind it, and the County Clerk answers for deeds and for overdue bills.

  • Sheriff: 135 W Irvine, Suite B01, Richmond, reached at 859-623-1511. Bills can be searched and paid through a secure portal, at the counter, or by post, and cash should never go in an envelope.
  • PVA: appraisals and exemption paperwork. The sheriff's tax page lists 859-623-5410 for it.
  • Clerk: deeds are filed at the Richmond Branch, 321 N. Madison Ave. The Berea branch on Chestnut Street (number 304) serves vehicle and marriage license customers.

An heir or agent can settle a bill ahead of a sale too, because KRS 134.119 lets the sheriff accept money from a third party for the owner.

sections.h2: Why does Madison County differ from the rural counties around it?
sections.html:
Madison County is a college county that has been adding residents for decades. Eastern Kentucky University is in Richmond, Berea College is in Berea, and Berea and Richmond are the county's only cities. Census counts show the effect: 28,541 people in 1940, 53,352 in 1980, 82,916 in 2010 and 92,701 in 2020, with the July 2025 estimate at 101,696.

The Transylvania Company bought some 20,000,000 acres west of the Appalachians from the Cherokee in 1774, and hired Daniel Boone to cut a trail through the Cumberland Gap and found a settlement on the Kentucky River. Settlement of the area began in the 1770s, and the county itself dates to December 1785, honoring James Madison. Fort Boonesborough, begun in April 1775, is today a state historic site. Interstate 75, U.S. 25, U.S. 421 and KY 52 cross the county, which borders Fayette County to the north and Jessamine, Garrard, Rockcastle, Jackson, Estill and Clark counties around the rest of its edge.

The 2020 census found 36,148 households, with renters in 40.5 percent of occupied units and 8.1 percent of all units vacant. Roughly 36 percent of residents were rural, which means plenty of sellers own land around Kingston, Waco or Speedwell rather than inside a city.

Appraisal of a farm follows what its soil earns, and a subdivision developer's offer plays no part. That is the rule in Section 172A of the state constitution. Ask the PVA to show how each of your acres is classified before you price a farm.

sections.h2: How big is the Madison County housing market?
sections.html:
The 2020 to 2024 survey period puts the median owner-occupied value at $232,000.

Between the April 2020 base and July 2025 the county added 9.7 percent. Its 1,808 employer establishments paid about $1.19 billion in 2023, and shoppers spent $1.76 billion in stores during 2022. A broadband subscription reaches 88.9 percent of households.

The age profile is young. Median age at the 2020 census was 35.6 years, and 20.4 percent of today's residents are under 18 against 16.1 percent who are 65 or older. In earlier decades the county jumped by more than a quarter in the 1970 and 1980 counts. Veterans number 5,522. Households run 2.43 people, and 84.2 percent of residents stayed at the same address for the past year. Per capita income is $32,828, and 16.4 percent of residents fall below the poverty line. Land is getting busier: 212.0 people per square mile in 2020 against 189.6 in 2010.

sections.h2: When does a Madison County tax bill start costing extra?
sections.html:
The sheriff's tax page gives no fixed calendar. It tells owners to trust the periods shown on their own bill or in the portal. The ordinary timetable sits in KRS 134.015.

  • Paying everything by November 1 earns two percent off.
  • The following two months, through December, call for the face amount.
  • During January a five percent charge appears.
  • From February onward the charge is ten percent of the unpaid tax.

A late-printed bill gets a compressed schedule from the Department of Revenue, counted from the mailing date. Fees pile onto delinquent bills, and the state's collection guide adds one percent interest per month after the transfer to the clerk.

On the Clerk's website you will find the 2025 delinquent county property tax list, split in two parts and marked updated August 31, 2026, along with a third-party purchaser page. Search for your parcel before you list. The County Attorney's office also runs delinquent collection and says an installment agreement signed before the Clerk's sale keeps a bill from being bought by an investor. Its number is 624-4777, extension 9.

sections.h2: What is the route for disputing a Madison County valuation?
sections.html:
A sit-down with the PVA comes first. When it settles nothing, you file a petition at the Clerk's office and the county board takes the case, as laid out in KRS 133.120 which the legislature revised effective July 15, 2026. Carry sales data, an appraisal or insurance records, and keep paying on your own number during the dispute.

Close to either campus, nearby recent sales of similar houses make the strongest comparables. On acreage, ask which agricultural class the PVA applied. KRS 133.030 has the board meet between 25 and 35 days following inspection.

sections.h2: Does Madison County offer a senior or disability homestead exemption?
sections.html: It does. The deduction for 2025 and 2026 is $49,100, which would lower a $232,000 home to a taxable $182,900. It is open to owner-occupants who are 65 or older or classified as totally disabled, and the Madison County PVA takes the application. A buyer who qualifies files separately after closing.

sections.h2: What should be settled before a Madison County closing?
sections.html:
Get a payoff figure from the sheriff for this year's bill and scan the clerk's delinquent list for earlier years. The sheriff's page notes that property taxes are commonly prorated between buyer and seller, with the current owner answerable for payment, so check how your settlement statement divides the bill.

A tax lien can ride with the land for as long as eleven years under KRS 134.015(5), which is why title agents ask for payoff at the table.

Deeds go to the Clerk's Richmond Branch at (859) 624-4703, extension 3. The office keeps papers from 1786 onward, searchable by a person's name only, and has scanned everything since 1986 for viewing in person or through the paid ECCLIX service. Electronic filings are handled each morning until roughly 10:00. Owners can also enroll in DocAlert, a free notification that fires whenever a document is recorded under their name or property details. The state's transfer tax, fifty cents for each $500 of value under KRS 142.050, comes to $232 at the Census median value.

faqs.q: Can Madison County property tax be paid online?
faqs.a: Yes, through the sheriff's secure portal, which also lets you search bills. The portal displays any processing fee before you confirm, and paying at the Richmond office or by mail still works.

faqs.q: How large is the 2026 exemption for Madison County seniors?
faqs.a: $49,100, the same as for 2025. Owners 65 or older, or totally disabled, apply through the PVA.

faqs.q: Which Madison County office records a deed?
faqs.a: The Clerk's Richmond Branch at 321 N. Madison Ave. Call (859) 624-4703, extension 3, for the recordings desk.

faqs.q: Is there help when a Madison County bill has gone delinquent?
faqs.a: The County Attorney's delinquent tax program, at 624-4777 extension 9, can arrange installment payments if you sign before the Clerk's sale.

faqs.q: Who pays the Madison County tax bill when a house changes owners mid-year?
faqs.a: The sheriff says the current owner must make sure it is paid and that bills are commonly prorated at closing. Confirm the split with your closing agent.
